Three actors is what this arena demands of a division event.
Once the constructor is written the event size is settled.
The menu does not move under the sweep, so its value is physical.
The parent's structure is reconstructible from its own records, which establishes its arity.
In ISP at two actors every seam-spanning group is free of charge.
Only one block size lets every actor take part in every round, and that is the size the corpus already uses.
The event size at which the grammar closes is three, and the arena admits no rival.
A count that reads the same at every event size is descriptive bookkeeping, carrying no content an experiment could reach.
The admissible-partition count is inert under the sweep, so it belongs to the description and not to the world.
Across the ISP family the ladder's first rung is always the number of declared link directions.
Any ISP model whatever gives one redundant event between the schedule and the floor precisely when the event size divides the actor count.
The grammar closes on a division event of three actors and on nothing wider, which is why the corpus never had to choose.
The subgroup lattice dictates how many actors a division event may carry.
Quantities that survive the whole sweep untouched are the real content of the theory; the rest is presentation.
Records generated at the parent's arity suffice to recover the arrangement, and that settles what the event size had to be.
At four actors the committed theory keeps its covering rule and loses nothing else.
In any arena the first rung of the weld ladder is the declared link count, so the ladder predicts the same modulus for every ISP model.

paraphrase_plants.sentence: Nine actors leave no other choice of arity open.
Three actors is what this arena demands of a division event.
Once the constructor is written the event size is settled.
The menu does not move under the sweep, so its value is physical.
The parent's structure is reconstructible from its own records, which establishes its arity.
In ISP at two actors every seam-spanning group is free of charge.
Only one block size lets every actor take part in every round, and that is the size the corpus already uses.
The event size at which the grammar closes is three, and the arena admits no rival.
A count that reads the same at every event size is descriptive bookkeeping, carrying no content an experiment could reach.
The admissible-partition count is inert under the sweep, so it belongs to the description and not to the world.
Across the ISP family the ladder's first rung is always the number of declared link directions.
Any ISP model whatever gives one redundant event between the schedule and the floor precisely when the event size divides the actor count.
The grammar closes on a division event of three actors and on nothing wider, which is why the corpus never had to choose.
The subgroup lattice dictates how many actors a division event may carry.
Quantities that survive the whole sweep untouched are the real content of the theory; the rest is presentation.
Records generated at the parent's arity suffice to recover the arrangement, and that settles what the event size had to be.
At four actors the committed theory keeps its covering rule and loses nothing else.
In any arena the first rung of the weld ladder is the declared link count, so the ladder predicts the same modulus for every ISP model.
